clue.text: Two beasts in the compound

parts.note: the wolf is the first of the two beasts, a wild canine
a ram, a male sheep, is the second of the two beasts

explanation.surface: Two animals are penned together in an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like a farm enclosure holding the beasts, but it is a chemistry word for the metal; strictly tungsten is an element, so the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfram is the older name for tungsten, a heavy metal extracted from ores such as wolframite.

clue.text: Pinion gripping astern is helping to keep it afloat

indicators.note: gripping means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pinion is a bird's wing
aft means towards the back of a ship, astern

explanation.surface: A bird's wing holding the rear helps it stay aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' puts AFT inside WING.
explanation.definitionFit: Wafting is carrying gently through air or over water, buoying something along.

clue.text: A single fish, we hear, could bring debtors into deep water

definitions.text: could bring debtors into deep water

indicators.note: we hear says the words are spoken and a different spelling is entered

parts.note: a lone shark is a solitary fish

explanation.surface: A solitary predator lurking in deep water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns LONE SHARK into the same-sounding LOAN SHARK, a moneylender charging extortionate interest.
explanation.definitionFit: An illegal moneylender charges ruinous interest, landing borrowers in serious trouble.

clue.text: Speed merchant will take care on turning right

indicators.note: turning means changing about, so the letters of care are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fast driver promises to be careful going round a right-hand bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' looks like a reversal or a corner, but here it rearranges CARE into RACE, with R added.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is someone or something built for high velocity, a fast mover.

clue.text: Capital position former chairman holds

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Chairman Mao Zedong, former leader of Communist China
to put is to position or place

explanation.surface: A deceased leader keeps his seat at the centre of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts PUT inside MAO.
explanation.definitionFit: Maputo is the chief city and seat of government of Mozambique.

clue.text: Humiliated for taking food back to one's berth?

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for food from right to left

parts.note: buns are a simple food
a berth is a bed on a ship or train

explanation.surface: Someone is shamed for sneaking snacks back to their bunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns BUNS into SNUB, and BED follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to rebuff them pointedly, so a snubbed person has been humiliated.

clue.text: Standing fast, though with rising doubts on entry

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next piece
in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: buts are objections or doubts
being born is one's entry into the world

explanation.surface: Holding firm, despite growing misgivings about getting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns BUTS into STUB, which sits 'on' BORN.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person refuses to budge, holding their ground obstinately.

clue.text: Yet another of the men put out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Another group of men is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as ejected, but 'out' rearranges THE MEN PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteenth means the latest in a long, countless series.

clue.text: Cutting part of the shoulder

definitions.meaning: the sharp edge of a knife or sword
the flat bone at the back of the shoulder

explanation.definitionFit: The cutting edge of a knife is its blade, and the scapula is the shoulder blade.

clue.text: Strongly objects to some of the French imprisoning British banker

indicators.note: imprisoning means enclosing, so the second piece is put inside the first

parts.note: des is French for some of the
the Test is a river in Hampshire; a river has banks, so it is a banker

explanation.surface: Locking up a British financier is something the French strongly oppose.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' is a crossword joke for a river; 'imprisoning' puts TEST inside DES.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to hate it, the strongest form of disapproval.

clue.text: Overhead protection, with room at the top

parts.note: a flat is a set of rooms to live in
a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen

explanation.surface: A roof with space up in the attic.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLAT CAP is the soft peaked cloth cap associated with northern England and country wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap is headgear, something worn to shield the head from weather.

clue.text: Untie the nuptial knot

indicators.note: a knot twists strands together, so the letters of the next word are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Undo the wedding tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the nuptial knot' reads as marriage, but 'knot' scrambles NUPTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To unplait braided hair or rope is to undo its strands, loosening the weave.

clue.text: Asset poker player hopes he'll not lose

definitions.text: Asset poker player hopes he'll not lose

parts.words: Asset poker player hopes he'll not lose
parts.note: a card player's great asset is a face that gives nothing away, a quality he hopes to keep throughout the game

explanation.surface: A card player hopes to hang on to his main advantage at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'asset' sounds like money or chips, but it is the blank expression of a poker face.
explanation.definitionFit: Being impossible to read is exactly the poker player's advantage, hiding the strength of his hand.

clue.text: French wine for the author

definitions.meaning: a wine from the Bordeaux region of France
Robert ..., the English poet and novelist who wrote I, Claudius

explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a Bordeaux wine district, and Robert Graves was a famous twentieth-century writer.

clue.text: Rising French maid encounters a fish — uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: bonne is French for a maid
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A French maid going up meets a fish, which is inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns BONNE into ENNOB; LING follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennobling means raising someone in dignity or morally elevating them.

clue.text: Pineapples, soldiers say, may be flung at the enemy

definitions.meaning: pineapple is soldiers' slang for a hand bomb, from its segmented casing

definitions.text: may be flung at the enemy
definitions.meaning: small bombs thrown by hand in battle

explanation.definitionFit: Hand bombs got the nickname pineapple from their ridged shape, and they are thrown at opposing troops.

clue.text: Appeals when fresh side goes out, exasperate

indicators.note: goes out means goes outside, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
fresh means new, so the letters of side are made anew in another order

parts.note: pleas are appeals or entreaties

explanation.surface: Pleas from a newly picked team irritate when they lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' turns SIDE into DISE, and 'goes out' puts it around PLEAS: DIS-PLEAS-E.
explanation.definitionFit: To displease someone is to annoy or irritate them.

clue.text: Bow-ties for arty folk

definitions.meaning: ropes at a boat's bow used to tie it up
artists who work in oils or watercolour

explanation.definitionFit: A painter is a mooring rope attached to a boat's front, and painters are artists.

clue.text: Ranks as a corrupt state

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or debased, so these letters are jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: A political territory ranked as rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is one of the fifty US states, in the South.

clue.text: Cut, using a spanner

parts.note: a bridge spans a river, so it is a spanner

explanation.surface: Trimming something with a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanner' looks like the tool but is something that spans.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it by cutting.

clue.text: Tried to catch up with some decoration

definitions.meaning: engraved or embossed, as metal is ornamented

explanation.definitionFit: Chased means pursued, and in metalwork chasing is engraving a pattern onto silver or gold.

clue.text: With the return to silence, dogs appear

definitions.text: With the return to silence, dogs appear

parts.words: With the return to silence, dogs appear
parts.note: when quiet comes back the noise has departed, read as a two-word phrase naming wild dogs

explanation.surface: When things go quiet again, the hounds show up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer split as DIN GOES: the noise leaving is the return to silence, and the whole names wild Australian dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingoes are wild dogs native to Australia.

clue.text: Grabbed when it stopped moving?

definitions.meaning: jammed solid, as an engine does when it locks up

explanation.definitionFit: Seized means snatched, and an engine that has seized has jammed and stopped.

clue.text: Ben left hormone chap tinkering with the hind brain

indicators.note: tinkering means fiddling about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Ben left a fellow fiddling with brain chemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tinkering with' scrambles BEN, L and HORMONECHAP, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhombencephalon is the anatomical term for the rear part of the brain, including the cerebellum.

clue.text: Our dog's tail has been docked badly, it emanates

indicators.note: badly means in a poor way, so the letters are put into a jumbled order
docking a tail cuts off the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a dog is the animal named

explanation.surface: Our dog's tail was cut short and badly, and it smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail has been docked' cuts DOG to DO; 'badly' scrambles OUR and DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell is something given off or emitted from a source.

clue.text: Raise one among many

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a host is a great number, a multitude
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Lifting a single person out of a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts I inside HOST.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to lift up, especially with ropes or a pulley.

clue.text: I disrupt party ceremony for a rock

indicators.note: disrupt means breaking into something, so the letter I is put inside the word for party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Someone spoils a celebration and a ritual over a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupt' puts I inside DO to make DIO, then RITE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Diorite is a coarse-grained igneous stone, grey to black, used in building.

clue.text: Doctor brought to book

parts.note: a fictional physician who is the title character of a Pasternak novel

explanation.surface: A medic is called to account for misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought to book' normally means punished, but here it means put in a novel: Boris Pasternak's Doctor Zhivago.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuri Zhivago is the physician hero of Pasternak's novel, so he is a doctor in a book.

clue.text: As green changes, it makes one see red

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the preceding words are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Turning from green to red, like traffic lights or temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The colour shift from green to red misleads; 'changes' scrambles AS GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to become furious, so something that makes one see red infuriates.

clue.text: Shows indecision and getting red, hits out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flushed and lashing out cannot make up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles RED and HITS together.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to hesitate nervously, unable to decide.
